But rule 8 says don't fabricate; including it is fine. I'll include accuracy_class with value "III, IIII".

- Fraction of the maximum permissible error: 0 → this is p_ind? Actually for indicators, fraction of max permissible error = 0.5? Here it says 0. I'll use "fraction_of_maximum_permissible_error" with value 0.

Hmm, actually for digital load cell configuration, p_i = 0? For a digital indicator the fraction of the MPE allotted is typically 0.5 for analog, 0 for digital. Fine, value 0.

- Weighing range: Single interval → value: "Single interval" string, attribute: weighing_range
- Power supply voltage: 110 – 240 V AC 50/60 Hz → split into:

  - power_supply_frequency: {min:50, max:60}, unit Hz
  - power_supply_type: "AC"
- Software identification: Version number: v0.1 or v0.2 → attribute: software_identification / software_version_number, value "v0.1 or v0.2". I'll use software_version with value "v0.1 or v0.2"? canonical label: software_version_number. Hmm, maybe "software_identification": {value: "v0.1 or v0.2"}. I'll do software_version_number: {value: "v0.1 or v0.2"}? The table cell says "Version number: v0.1 or v0.2." So attribute software_version_number, value "v0.1 or v0.2". Remove trailing period.

The markdown doesn't mention module designation. I'll omit.

Model family: only one model, so omit per rule ("include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant").

Config: "Digital load cells" — this is a characteristic, put type_level "load_cell_configuration": {value: "Digital load cells"}? Or component? It's just a description of configuration. I'll include as type_level characteristic: configuration → value "Digital load cells". Canonical: load_cell_interface: "Digital load cells". I'll use "configuration": value "Digital load cells"? Hmm "Configuration" is the label. Canonical snake_case: "configuration". Value "Digital load cells".
